title: Maple, Pecan and Cranberry Pancakes
changes_from_base: Wholemeal and almond flour replace the plain flour, sweetened only with a spoonful of maple syrup in the batter, with chopped pecans and dried cranberries folded through.
summary: Nutty wholemeal and almond flour pancakes studded with pecans and dried cranberries, sweetened with a touch of maple syrup.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
butter or oil, for the pan

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Sift the 140 g wholemeal flour, 60 g almond flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and ¼ tsp salt together.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 2 eggs, then whisk in the 1 tbsp maple syrup, 360 ml buttermilk, 2 tbsp rapeseed oil and 1 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Quickly whisk the flour mix into the wet ingredients, then fold in the 60 g pecans and 60 g dried cranberries without overworking.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat a griddle over medium-high heat and brush with butter or oil.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drop 3-4 tbsp batter per pancake onto the hot griddle.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When bubbles break through, slide a spatula carefully underneath, as the pancakes are delicate, flip and cook for about 1 min more until brown underneath.

tips: Fold in the pecans and cranberries gently so the batter stays light.
These pancakes are softer than standard ones, so flip them carefully with a thin spatula.
A splash of maple syrup in the batter means they need little extra at the table.
storage: Serve straight away, or once cool, wrap portions in cling film and freeze in a freezer bag. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
